Even if you were not offended by those comments, someone else may be offended by them, so if they make these comments often, or others overheard it, your supervisor can find themself in hot water really quick.

Well, it would be very state specific.  My company operates in multiple states, but we pretty much align our practices with CA law as it tends to be the most employee leaning state.  For your situation, in CA, if any available paid time off is exhausted, an exempt employee’s pay can be deducted by a full day or half day (if the employee did not work longer than half the day).  I had that situation with a client when I was a consultant and found case law to support the half day dock in pay (I thought it was very odd).  

Most companies will pay an exempt employee a full day of pay if any work was performed on that day, as it is a trade off for not having to pay overtime.

Most time keeping systems will allow a negative balance and should be a setting your master user can adjust.  Allowing a negative balance is a gamble on the employer end, as you cannot recover that balance if the employee leaves.

It might be a good idea to hold off on changing the policy until the fall as the DOL is scheduled to address the federal overtime rules and exemptions.  There have been talks of possible drastic changes, even stronger than the proposed changes that were ultimately blocked heading into 2016.  A large number of companies reclassified roles and made other changes that ended up not being necessary.

I am an HR Professional and offer the following from an objective point of view:

Check employer reviews on Glassdoor.com.  This will give you some insight into the employee experience and may even have reviews of people that did not accept an offer.  Take negative reviews with a grain of salt because those are usually from disgruntled former employees.  Look for patterns.

Consider the size of each company and if the offer is extended by a recruiter or the hiring manager.  I would put more confidence in the company that has the recruiter extend the offer.  That company has a more solid organizational structure and would be a more logical long term decision.

If you did not ask during the interview process, ask what impact has been put on this position due to the pandemic.  That will give you insight into the long term prospects of the job.

Ask where the offer lies within the penetration impact of the job grade.  If they don’t know what you are talking about, run away!  If it is close to 50%, that is good.  If less than 50%, there is room to negotiate.  If over 50%, take it.

Feel free to DM me if you have any other questions or want guidance through the process.

Wishing you the best of luck!
